en: translated by Kumārajīva, the Tripiṭaka Master from India during the Yao Qin Dynasty.
When the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara was practicing the profound Prajñāpāramitā, he clearly perceived the five aggregates.
Emptiness delivers one from all suffering and calamity.

“Śāriputra, because form is empty, it has no characteristic of affliction or disintegration; because sensation is empty, it has no characteristic of being felt; because perception is empty, it has no characteristic of cognition; because formations are empty, they have no characteristic of volitional activity; because consciousness is empty, it has no characteristic of awareness.”
form is not different from emptiness, and emptiness is not different from form.
Form is emptiness, and emptiness is form.
Feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are also like this. "Śāriputra!
All these dharmas have the characteristic of emptiness: they are neither born nor extinguished, neither defiled nor pure, neither increasing nor decreasing.
This dharma of emptiness is not of the past, not of the future, and not of the present.

Therefore, in emptiness there is no form, no sensation, perception, mental formations, or consciousness; no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind; no forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or phenomena; no眼界 (eye-element) up to and including no意識界 (consciousness-element); no ignorance and no end of ignorance, up to and including no old age and death and no end of old age and death; no suffering, accumulation, cessation, or path; and no wisdom and no attainment.
Because there is nothing to be apprehended, the Bodhisattva relies on the Prajñāpāramitā, and thus his mind is without hindrance.
Because he is without hindrance, he has no fear; he is far removed from all perverted dreams and delusions and suffering, and attains ultimate Nirvāṇa.
The Buddhas of the three periods of time, by relying on the Prajñāpāramitā, have attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Therefore, know that the Prajñāpāramitā is the great mantra of illumination, the unsurpassed mantra of illumination, the unequaled mantra of illumination; it is able to eliminate all suffering, being true and not false.
He then spoke the mantra, saying:
"Gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā. The Mahāprajñāpāramitā-mahāvidyā-mantra-sūtra.
